articles.headline: Jayden Daniels, Commanders 'keep fighting through adversity,' improve to 2-4-1
articles.description: After falling behind 10-0 in the first half, quarterback Jayden Daniels led the Washington Commanders on a rousing rally, cruising to a 27-10 win over the Philadelphia Eagles at Northwest Stadium, an effort in which he threw for 217 yards and a touchdown.
articles.headlineJa: ジェイデン・ダニエルズとコマンダーズ、「逆境に立ち向かい続ける」、戦績を2勝4敗1分けに
articles.descriptionJa: 前半に10-0のリードを許した後、クォーターバックのジェイデン・ダニエルズがワシントン・コマンダーズを力強い猛追へと導き、ノースウェスト・スタジアムでのフィラデルフィア・イーグルス戦を27-10で快勝した。ダニエルズは217ヤードのパスと1タッチダウンを記録した。
articles.body:
LANDOVER, MD. -- The last time Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels won a start before Sunday night's 27-10 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles, he had yet to dislocate his elbow and had not endured questions about his durability or his game.

When asked if it felt like it had been a year since his last win -- it was Oct. 5, 2025 to be exact -- Daniels said, "It probably felt longer."

That's why he wanted to savor Sunday's win, during which he completed 16 of 29 passes for 217 yards and a touchdown. He also ran for 23 yards. He completed passes for 53 and 30 yards in the second half to help Washington earn its second win of the season. The Commanders are 2-4-1 and two games behind the first-place Giants in the NFC East.

Since that win over the Chargers last year, Daniels had endured several adverse situations.

He fumbled the following week, leading to a Bears comeback win; he missed a game because of a hamstring injury; he dislocated his left elbow and missed three games aggravated it upon his return, causing him to be shut down for the final four games.

Then, in 2026, he missed two games after dislocating the elbow again, and in his last game at home, he failed to throw the ball out of bounds to stop the clock in overtime, preventing the Commanders from kicking a last-second field goal to snap a tie against the Giants.

He was 0-7-1 in his previous eight starts -- though he failed to finish four of those outings. Before that stretch, he had won 15 of his first 20 regular-season starts.

"It's a blessing," Daniels said, "just to go out there and everything I've been through in my career so far, just to keep pushing and keep fighting through adversity to come out with a big-time win with these guys and knowing I could have had a different direction."

Daniels' season could've ended after dislocating his elbow in Week 2. But he finished his third consecutive game since the injury. He has thrown six touchdown passes and no interceptions this season and has run for two more scores.

"You make those sacrifices because guys are putting everybody on the line," said Daniels, who had the wind knocked out of him on a hit late in the first half. "Who am I to not do the same thing?"

Washington coach Dan Quinn wasn't surprised.

"He showed a lot of toughness," Quinn said. "He took a real shot toward the end of the first half. To see him [go], 'I'm good,' and he comes back and then made a bunch of plays. ... I always feel [his] poise and control."

Daniels also displayed his evolving leadership. In Washington's first three series, the Commanders committed four penalties, missed a 55-yard field goal attempt, had one three-and-out and lost a fumble. After the turnover, Daniels gathered most of the offensive players on the sidelines for an inspirational lecture.

articles.headline: Saquon Barkley has assurances he won't be dealt, wants to help Eagles 'fix it'
articles.description: Speaking after Sunday night's 27-10 loss to the Washington Commanders, Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley told reporters he has received assurances from the front office that he will remain with the club beyond the Nov. 10 trade deadline.
articles.headlineJa: サクオン・バークリー、放出されないとの確約を得る、イーグルスの「立て直し」を助けたい意向
articles.descriptionJa: 日曜夜のワシントン・コマンダーズ戦で27-10で敗れた後、フィラデルフィア・イーグルスのランニングバック、サクオン・バークリーは記者団に対し、11月10日のトレード期限を過ぎてもチームに残留するとフロントから確約を得たと語った。
articles.body:
LANDOVER, MD. -- Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley said he has received assurances from the front office that he will remain with the team beyond the Nov. 10 trade deadline.

"When that message was relayed to me, it definitely does mean a lot," Barkley said after Sunday night's 27-10 loss to the Washington Commanders.

"The whole time my mindset was, we have a little issue going on right now and I feel like I'm the type of player and the type of leader that can help us get out of it, and I want to be one of the reasons why we fix it."

The Eagles have lost six straight games and are now 2-6 this season. They have one game remaining before the trade deadline, at home against the NFC East-leading New York Giants next Sunday.

Howie Roseman has been among the most active general managers when it comes to trades during his tenure and has already made what can be considered a "sell" move by dealing offensive lineman Cam Jurgens and a 2027 seventh-round pick to the Baltimore Ravens in October for a 2027 fifth-round pick and 2028 second-rounder.

More losses have piled up since then, and with them have come questions about whether Philadelphia will continue to explore moving players for draft capital.

Barkley said he "really didn't read too much into" the social media speculation about his future but appreciated the backing of the front office.

"I have nothing but respect for this organization, top to bottom. I really do think they do things the right way," he said. "It's an honor and a privilege every single time I get to go out there and play for this organization and put on the midnight green."

Barkley, who has been dealing with hamstring and back injuries, once again had his snaps limited against the Commanders. He played 22 of a possible 68 plays and ended with 14 touches for 54 yards and a touchdown.

articles.headline: Jayden Daniels throws TD pass and Commanders shut out Eagles over final 3 quarters in 27-10 win
articles.description: — The Washington Commanders had just under two weeks to sit with their disheartening start to the season before their matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday night.
articles.headlineJa: ジェイデン・ダニエルズがTDパスを決め、コマンダーズが残り3クォーターを無失点に抑えて27-10で勝利
articles.descriptionJa: ワシントン・コマンダーズは、日曜夜のフィラデルフィア・イーグルス戦を前に、シーズン序盤の不本意なスタートを整理するための期間を2週間弱持っていた。
articles.body:
LANDOVER, Md. -- — The Washington Commanders had just under two weeks to sit with their disheartening start to the season before their matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday night.


              Coming off a bye week, they still needed an extra 10 or so minutes.


              Washington pulled together after an extraordinarily sloppy first quarter to score 27 straight points in a 27-10 victory. It was Washington’s first win in more than a month, and Philadelphia’s sixth straight loss.


              “When you come off of a bye, you either rev right up or you need a minute to warm up — and we took a minute,” Washington coach Dan Quinn said.


              The Commanders (2-4-1) committed a bevy of first-quarter penalties, which put them behind 10-0.


              Jayden Daniels threw for 217 yards and a touchdown, as the offense got rolling. Aided by a defense that pitched a shutout for the final three-plus quarters, Daniels had time to build rapport with his receivers absent Terry McLaurin. The victory was Daniels’ first as a starter since beating the Los Angeles Chargers on Oct. 5, 2025.


              “It’s a blessing from God just to go out there, and everything I’ve been through in my career so far,” Daniels said. “From different injuries and a lot of different setbacks."


              The Commanders sacked Tanner McKee five times and intercepted one of his passes while holding the Eagles to 268 yards — just 199 before the meaningless final drive.


              In his third start of the season in place of the injured Jalen Hurts, McKee threw for 212 yards without a touchdown. And prior to the final drive of the game, the Eagles' longest drive was 52 yards.


              “We just made adjustments,” cornerback Trey Amos said. “We started a little bit slow, those things will happen sometimes, but after those adjustments, everybody came together to try and figure out a plan. It worked out, later down the line, series, quarters.”


              Saquon Barkley ran for a touchdown for the Eagles but was held to 30 yards on 13 carries. Philadelphia finished with 91 yards rushing.


              “I know nobody feels sorry for us, that’s for damn sure,” coach Nick Sirianni said. “Everyone is going to give us their best shot. I know nobody feels sorry for us and we have to do everything we can do to fix it so we don’t have this feeling for the last six games. Obviously, it sucks."


              Both teams committed costly penalties. The Eagles’ Jake Elliott made a field goal to cut Washington’s lead to three points in the fourth quarter, but he had to try again because of an illegal formation penalty and missed from 41 yards.


              Drew Stevens kicked four field goals for Washington, including a 56-yarder late in the first quarter. Daniels connected with Stefon Diggs for an 8-yard touchdown strike in the second quarter that tied it at 10l, and Washington led 13-10 at halftime.

articles.description: Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering the biggest questions coming out of each Sunday game. Here's what we learned from Week 8.
articles.headlineJa: NFL第8週：日曜の試合から見る重要事項、疑問点、ファンタジー視点の分析
articles.descriptionJa: NFL Nationのレポーター陣がすべての試合展開に反応し、日曜日の各試合から生じた最大の疑問に答えます。第8週のまとめをお届けします。
articles.body:
The Sunday slate for Week 8 of the 2026 NFL season kicked off with some shocking results in the early window, including two overtime finishes.

Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson injured his right thumb on his first snap back after missing three games with an ankle injury, allowing the Bills to cruise to an easy win. The Vikings lost their first game of the season, scoring just 15 points against a Lions defense that had allowed 20-plus points five times in 2026. And despite not completing a pass, the Buccaneers shut out the Falcons.

In the late window Sunday, the Chargers lost in an L.A. showdown versus the Rams. It marked the third time that quarterback Justin Herbert threw multiple interceptions (two) this season.

Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering lingering questions coming out of each game and detailing everything else you need to know. Fantasy football analysts Matt Bowen and Tristan Cockcroft also have fantasy takeaways from each matchup.

Let's get to it with the biggest lessons from Sunday.

Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Patriots

Can Patriots sustain playing this way? The first half was their worst of the season (just 98 yards on offense), and while they exploded in the second half, they might not be as fortunate in the next two weeks against better competition -- home against the Packers and then against the Lions in Munich, Germany. The big play bailed them out, with quarterback Drake Maye -- who was excellent while facing heavy pressure -- throwing touchdown passes to Kyle Williams (43 yards) and DeMario Douglas (48-yard catch-and-run). It was the Patriots' first game with multiple receiving TDs of 40-plus yards since Sept. 24, 2017, versus the Texans.

Trend to watch: Injuries impacting the Patriots' roster. Starting tight end Hunter Henry (foot) left the game in the first half and didn't return, while promising rookie outside linebacker Gabe Jacas (knee) left the game in the third quarter and did not return. The team already entered the game without starting wide receiver A.J. Brown (knee) and No. 2 running back TreVeyon Henderson (illness). -- Mike Reiss

Next game: vs. Packers (Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET)

Dolphins

For a team still learning how to win, what lesson can the Dolphins take away from today's game? Mainly that games are not over until they're over, which is a lesson this young Dolphins team got an introduction to in last week's win over the Jets. articles.headline: Kerim Alajbegovic and Jérémie Boga hit stunners as Juventus beat 10-man Napoli
articles.description: Kerim Alajbegovic and Jérémie Boga scored stunning second-half goals as Juventus beat 10-man Napoli 2-0 at the Allianz Stadium to ease the pressure on head coach Luciano Spalletti.
articles.headlineJa: ケリム・アライベゴビッチとジェレミー・ボガが鮮烈なゴール、ユヴェントスが10人となったナポリを下す
articles.descriptionJa: アリアンツ・スタジアムで行われた試合で、ケリム・アライベゴビッチとジェレミー・ボガが後半に素晴らしいゴールを決め、ユヴェントスが10人となったナポリを2-0で破ってルチアーノ・スパレッティ監督へのプレッシャーを軽減した。
articles.body:
Kerim Alajbegovic and Jérémie Boga scored stunning second-half goals as Juventus beat 10-man Napoli 2-0 at the Allianz Stadium to ease the pressure on head coach Luciano Spalletti.

Juve, who had won only one of their four previous Serie A matches, had been jeered by their own fans earlier in the second period before Bosnian teenager Alajbegovic and Boga both struck with long-range efforts.

Napoli, who slipped to their fourth league defeat of the season, had defender Luca Marianucci sent off soon after Juve's opener for his second yellow card.

Napoli went close to taking an early lead as Lorenzo Lucca's early diving header was brilliantly saved by Juve goalkeeper Guglielmo Vicario.

Juve's first chance was blazed over the crossbar by Jhon Lucumí in the 16th minute and they went closer soon after when Colombia defender Juan Cabal's close-range effort hit a post.

Both sides continued to create chances before the break, but lacked quality in front of goal.

Scoring chances at both ends dried up after the restart and there were whistles and jeers from the home fans after Randal Kolo Muani's misplaced pass.

Juve skipper Bremer headed Douglas Luiz's cross straight at Alex Meret before Alajbegovic's first Serie A goal gave Juve supporters something to cheer as he slammed a 20-yard shot into the top corner.

Napoli were dealt a further blow five minutes later when centre-half Marianucci received his second yellow card for his rash challenge on Cabal.

And it got worse for the visitors when Boga, an earlier replacement for Alajbegovic, cut in from the left and curled a superb finish into the far corner.

articles.headline: Arteta says Arsenal 'loved the mission' in first Anfield win since 2012
articles.description: Mikel Arteta said his players "loved the mission" of winning at Liverpool for the first time in 14 years as he hailed Sunday's "historic" 1-0 victory at Anfield.
articles.headlineJa: アルテタ監督、2012年以来初のアニフィールド勝利に「ミッションを楽しんでいた」と語る
articles.descriptionJa: ミケル・アルテタ監督は、日曜日のアニフィールドでの「歴史的」な1-0の勝利を称賛し、選手たちが14年ぶりとなるリヴァプールでの勝利という「ミッションを楽しんでいた」と語った。
articles.body:
Mikel Arteta said his players "loved the mission" of winning at Liverpool for the first time in 14 years as he hailed Sunday's "historic" 1-0 victory at Anfield.

Kai Havertz's 16th-minute strike was enough to secure a narrow win in a hard-fought game that sent the Gunners three points clear at the top of the Premier League ahead of Manchester City.

Liverpool put Arsenal under huge pressure after falling behind, but the visitors kept them at bay with a more controlled second-half display, and the Reds ended without registering a shot on target for the first time ever in a Premier League home game.

Arsenal had lost eight of their past 13 league games and kept just one clean sheet in 27 previous league visits to Anfield before Sunday.

"[They are] just loving the mission," said Arteta. "And the mission was something that we didn't accomplish in 14 years. There were reasons for that. Some of them were psychological problems. Some of them were related to the quality that we showed on the pitch, certain moments or decisions.

"And we knew that we need to nail absolutely all of them. And we're going to have to navigate through periods that we're going to have to suffer because they are extremely good at doing that and creating those vertical attacks, those chaos moments for almost nothing.

"You really need to enjoy that. If you don't, there will be a moment they will switch up and they will punish you. And yeah, I think the way we competed and played and the chances that we generated as well, it was really impressive. So I'm really happy."

Arsenal, after being dumped out of the Carabao Cup by League Two side Fleetwood Town in midweek, responded with a defiant display to extend their record in the Premier League to eight wins and one loss from nine games.

"We're extremely proud of what the team, the players, everybody's done especially in the conditions that we arrived to this game, where we were after the defeat against Liverpool, it looks like the end of the world," Arteta said. "It looks like, 'Yeah, what are we doing?' And then you have to pick yourself up and understand that this is a beautiful part of this game.

"It can take you to really bad places, but four days later you have the opportunity to do something really historic, and we've done it."

articles.headline: Ex-Liverpool, Man City star Milner runs NYC Marathon in just over three hours
articles.description: It's clear James Milner is enjoying his retirement from soccer, as he ran the 2026 NYC Marathon on Sunday with an impressive time. Did we mention he's 40 years old?
articles.body:
James Milner has always been something of a cult hero in soccer, with his work ethic and personable demeanor making him a fan favorite across a 24-year career, especially at the clubs he represented. From Leeds United to Newcastle United, Aston Villa, Manchester City, Liverpool and Brighton, Milner made a career for being the hardest working, indefatigable presence in every team, routinely finishing tops of preseason fitness tests even as he celebrated turning 40 back in January.

He announced his retirement at the end of the 2025-26 season but do you think for one minute that "Milly" has taken it easier now that he's hung up his boots?

Of course he hasn't: On Sunday, he seemingly cruised his way through the 2026 New York City Marathon, completing the course in a remarkable 3:09.04. Not bad, James, not bad at all!

Looking deeper at his split times, it does seem as though Milner took it easy (well, easier) down the stretch, wrapping the first half in 1:31 before going 1:38 for the final 13 miles, but we forgive him for turning it into more of a fun run from there. That said, an average pace of 7:13 per mile is remarkable; it makes us tired just reading it.

What's next, Milner: climbing Mount Everest? Playing in the NFL? We wouldn't bet against him regardless of what he sets his sights on ...
